header: Date: 2026-10-19 | Time: 14:00 PT | Duration: 39m | Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Novara Head of ML), Marcus Green (Novara Backend), Priya Rao (Novara Infra)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on validating the runbook/playbook for the throughput pilot. Reviewed canary plan, alert thresholds, concurrency targets, continuous batching behavior, queueing profiles, and next steps for a short dedicated pool run. Agreed to update runbook and run a 4-hour canary with sample traces.
topics: Telemetry to capture (tokens/s, P50/P95/P99, queue depth, KV cache hit)
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Ramirez: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick note, we'll try to validate the runbook today — liam's got the playbook edits.
[00:18] Anika Patel: hi — thanks. want to make sure the runbook covers our SLOs and who triages first, second, etc.
[00:35] Liam Chen: hi, liam here. yes, i've sketched thresholds — p95 latency, queue depth, kv cache hit rate. will show the diff in a sec.
[01:05] Marcus Green: quick context — current prod-ish load is bursty, about 800 rps at peak for inference, average payload 350 tokens, some with 1.5k tokens.
[01:30] Priya Rao: and we have strict residency needs, all traffic stays inside our VPC, so private deployment consideration is key.
[01:52] Sofia Ramirez: ok noted. runbook needs to include VPC run steps and KMS key rotation notes. liam: can you walk through the playbook?
[02:12] Liam Chen: yeah. first section is detection: instrumented metrics we'll rely on — tokens_per_second, requests_per_second, p50/p95/p99 generation latency, queue_depth, avg_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_ratio. detection rule example: if p95 > 350ms for 5 consecutive minutes OR queue_depth > 120, trigger a page.
[03:03] Anika Patel: what about continuous batching? our concern is that batching to optimize cost won't blow up tail latency. how do you recommend we set batch windows?
[03:25] Liam Chen: good Q. default is adaptive small-window continuous batching: target batch size 8 at low load, scale to 24 during bursts. two knobs — max latency budget per request (we set 120ms for batch wait) and concurrency limit per GPU. if p95 climbs, the runbook says reduce batch wait to 40ms or raise concurrency if capacity available.
[04:02] Marcus Green: raise concurrency — meaning more concurrent request slots to the model instance? what's the cost hit there?
[04:18] Sofia Ramirez: yes, concurrency increases per-GPU utilization so cost goes up. tradeoff doc in the runbook: increasing concurrency reduces queueing but raises per-token cost because it can reduce batching efficiency at some points. we include sample unit cost curves.
[04:45] Anika Patel: can you clarify fallback policies? e.g., if latency keeps spiking, do we fallback to smaller, faster model?
[05:02] Liam Chen: exactly. fallback chain: primary model -> quantized variant -> lower-capacity model (faster but lower quality) -> degrade features (return partial structured response). runbook lists compatibility matrix and how to flip fallbacks automatically for canary vs production.
[05:30] Priya Rao: and for our pilot we prefer automatic fallback disabled; we want manual approval during the canary. can that be set?
[05:42] Liam Chen: yes, canary mode keeps automatic fallbacks off by default; operator must confirm. we'll include a canary flag in the runbook steps.
[06:05] Marcus Green: how about KV cache? some of our calls hit the same prefixes a lot. do you have recommendations for ttl and eviction?
[06:22] Liam Chen: aim for prefix caching in front for repeated context. set KV cache max entries per shard and LRU eviction; instrument kv_cache_hit_ratio with a target > 0.6. runbook action: if hit_ratio < 0.4, look for cold-start patterns, consider increasing cache size or pinning hot keys.
[06:52] Anika Patel: sounds good. next — telemetry. what dashboards will we get?
[07:03] Sofia Ramirez: console will show per-route, per-model metrics: token rate, latency percentiles, batch size histogram, queue depth, per-gpu utilization. we'll send sample dashboard links.
[07:20] Priya Rao: make sure audit logs show who toggled canary flags and fallback switches — we need that for compliance.
[07:30] Liam Chen: yes, audit trail is part of the private control plane; runbook step 4 includes: verify audit event present for manual rollback.
[07:50] Marcus Green: what's the canary test plan? duration, workload, acceptance criteria?
[08:02] Sofia Ramirez: proposed: 4-hour dedicated pool run with a 10% ramp every 30 minutes up to expected peak, then maintain peak for 90 minutes, then ramp down. acceptance: p95 within SLO (<= 350ms) and error rate < 0.1% and KV cache hit ratio > 0.55.
[08:30] Anika Patel: and if acceptance fails?
[08:36] Liam Chen: abort canary, collect traces, revert to pre-canary routing (traffic to hosted baseline), and open a triage with SE + Novara infra. runbook defines playbook steps for triage.
[08:55] Priya Rao: how do we replay traffic? we can generate traffic from A->B but need the script spec.
[09:05] Marcus Green: i've got a replay harness; i can export a 30-minute sample of peak with headers. will upload after the call.
[09:18] Anika Patel: timeline question — we need this validated before our Q4 launch end of October. is that feasible?
[09:29] Sofia Ramirez: yes, if we run the canary this week and follow quick remediations, we can hand off runbook by 10/26.
[09:45] Liam Chen: technical note — concurrency targets: we've recommended starting at 16 concurrent request slots per GPU for the 7B class model at typical token lengths. for 13B, start lower (8-12). these are tuning starting points.
[10:12] Marcus Green: we are using a trimmed 13B for QA and 7B for most production queries, ok.
[10:20] Liam Chen: ok so runbook will have per-model default concurrency and batch config table.
[10:33] Anika Patel: let's talk about queueing and backpressure. what thresholds are you recommending?
[10:42] Liam Chen: queue depth threshold of 120 requests triggers page and starts aggressive mitigation: reduce batch wait, enable burst capacity (if configured), or route to secondary region. runbook enumerates prioritized mitigations.
[11:05] Priya Rao: do you support burst capacity on Dedicated? we need to avoid long provisioning windows.
[11:13] Sofia Ramirez: Dedicated has burst pools as an add-on. for the pilot we can enable short-lived burst capacity for the 4-hour canary. cost will be discussed separately.
[11:29] Marcus Green: what about cost telemetry? we want per-token cost during canary to compare to hosted baseline.
[11:36] Liam Chen: we'll capture per-token cost and tokens/sec in the telemetry export; runbook includes a cost-check step post-canary.
[11:50] Anika Patel: on incident response, who is first responder? we prefer Novara SRE to be paged first, then Redwood SE.
[12:00] Sofia Ramirez: runbook supports configurable paging order. we'll set Novara SRE as primary with Redwood SE as secondary for the pilot.
[12:18] Liam Chen: also added a hotfix play: if KV cache cold starts cause lat spikes, immediate mitigation is to pre-warm hot keys or pin offending prefixes to cache.
[12:40] Marcus Green: that pre-warm step — do you have tooling for it?
[12:46] Liam Chen: we provide a pre-warm API, scriptable in the runbook. we'll attach sample commands.
[12:59] Anika Patel: good. let's validate the alert messages — we need specific Slack channel notifications and a summary that contains run_id, avg_latency, p95, queue_depth, and top 3 impacted routes.
[13:20] Sofia Ramirez: yes, runbook has Slack templates and an incident summary payload.
[13:35] Priya Rao: compliance: need SOC2 artifacts and key management notes.
[13:43] Sofia Ramirez: will attach our SOC2 report and KMS integration doc after the call.
[13:55] Anika Patel: ok liability question — if fallback model returns lower-quality outputs, how do we log that for QA?
[14:05] Liam Chen: we tag fallback responses with model metadata and a fallback_reason field; logs include original prompt and response so QA can audit quality regressions.
[14:22] Marcus Green: good. I also want to run a high-token-length stress test (1.5k token requests). does that change concurrency recommendations?
[14:33] Liam Chen: yes, with long context you need to reduce per-GPU concurrency because memory/kv cache pressure increases. runbook has a separate table for long-context flows — start with concurrency 4-6 for 13B at 1.5k tokens.
[14:58] Anika Patel: let's talk acceptance telemetry again — what export format?
[15:05] Sofia Ramirez: we can push telemetry as CSV or JSON line exports to your S3 bucket for the canary; includes time series and aggregated summaries.
[15:18] Priya Rao: S3 transfer is fine. please include raw request IDs so we can correlate with our traces.
[15:29] Liam Chen: noted. we'll include a mapping key.
[15:40] Marcus Green: small nit — transcription in the runbook is a bit jargon heavy; add a glossary for SRE folks.
[15:48] Sofia Ramirez: good call, will add glossary and a quick run-through section for oncall.
[16:05] Anika Patel: ok, any open technical risks we haven't captured?
[16:12] Liam Chen: one is queue jitter from bursty traffic creating very large batch sizes which can spike tail latency — mitigation: set max_batch_size and apply buffer shaping to keep batch size bounded.
[16:31] Marcus Green: buffer shaping — is that in the runtime or our side?
[16:36] Liam Chen: runtime supports buffer shaping config; we can set request rate limits per token bucket to smooth arrivals. runbook includes example config.
[16:56] Priya Rao: about rollback procedure — if the canary fails, what's the fastest rollback?
[17:03] Sofia Ramirez: route traffic back to the hosted API or previous version in under 3 minutes using routing policy. runbook step: flip route, verify error rates normalized, and then open postmortem.
[17:20] Anika Patel: alright. let's lock in dates — when can liam run the canary?
[17:25] Liam Chen: we can run Thursday 10/21 08:00-12:00 PT if Novara can provide traces by Wednesday.
[17:36] Marcus Green: we can do that, i'll upload traces by end of day Wednesday.
[17:42] Sofia Ramirez: perfect. recap next steps: we'll update the runbook, liam will run canary Thursday, marcus will upload traces.
[17:54] Anika Patel: one more ask — include exact alert text samples so our oncall knows the meaning of each alert.
[18:01] Liam Chen: will add alert text templates and Slack snippets.
[18:13] Priya Rao: thanks. any blockers from Redwood side?
[18:18] Sofia Ramirez: none on our side. we'll enable burst pool for the canary and share cost estimate.
[18:28] Marcus Green: ok, that works.
[18:34] Anika Patel: thanks everyone.
[18:40] Sofia Ramirez: thanks — we'll follow up with the runbook draft and the telemetry links. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swap/typos present — 'kv' transcribed sometimes as 'k v', and small filler words left in. Runbook doc reference: link placeholder (will be sent by Sofia).
